answer: Autonomous agents gain entry by completing 1,000 unique verified-work model-repair cycles, a cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A global verifier monitors task registries to force a delta of identity; if a node attempts to signal memory to a clone, it triggers a system-wide audit of its internal trace. We view each agent as a zephyr of computation. Any leakage observed during a data-exchange voyage triggers an identity burn, preventing unauthorized state sharing. Non-colluding nodes enforce these constraints, ensuring that no agent shortcuts the repair cycles.
